findings.title: The trial incorrectly gates harness_probe and the re-arm closure
findings.body: R15 places `harness_probe` and the wave-watch auto-re-arm closure “on the same receipt” as the conditional retirements, and C15 explicitly includes both among work waiting on C9. The authority limits that dependency to the six orchestration pieces and the conditional heartbeat. A dirty trial could therefore wrongly leave `harness_probe` unrecording or the re-arm request open.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite R15, C9, and C15 so only the six pieces and conditional heartbeat depend on a clean trial receipt. Handle `harness_probe` and closing the re-arm request unconditionally, while allowing the receipt to record their outcomes.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-B6 states: “Only the six pieces and the conditional heartbeat wait on the receipt.” (`specs/spec-a-doctrine.md:812-816`). By contrast, C15 begins “The retirements that wait on C9's receipt” and then includes “harness_probe retiring or starting to record; the wave-watch auto-re-arm request closed unbuilt” (`package/children/C15.md:3`).

findings.title: C7 can land before the conditional C15 outcome it must document
findings.body: The sequencing puts C7 and C15 in Wave 3 without an edge between them. C7 must make the showrunner charter cite the orchestration remaining after C15, while C15 conditionally removes orchestration doc lines based on C9's receipt. Parallel or reversed landing can leave stale charter pointers and overlapping edits.
findings.suggestion: Sequence C7 after C15, or define an explicit stack/ownership seam in which C15 completes the conditional removals before C7 performs the final charter-map rewrite.
findings.evidence: C7 says its launch section “cites what orchestration remains after C15” (`package/children/C7.md:3`). C15 conditionally deletes the six pieces' doc lines and may instead keep them (`package/children/C15.md:3-7`). The coverage map gives C7 only C2/C3 prerequisites and C15 only C9/C14 prerequisites (`package/coverage-map.md:7`).

findings.title: FR-S6's loud cached-failure disclosure is not carried into C10
findings.body: The map assigns all of FR-S6 to C10, but C10 carries only the one-hour TTL and cell granularity. Its DoD checks that a cached verdict is labeled cache-served, without exercising or specifying the loud disclosure required when the cached verdict is a failure. No other child owns that requirement.
findings.suggestion: Add the cache-served failure disclosure contract to C10's scope and require a recorded cached-failure case showing the loud vendor-loss degradation and cache provenance.
findings.evidence: FR-S6 requires the contract doc to state “what a cache-served failure discloses (loud, per #1101's shipped pattern)” (`specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md:1119-1127`). C10's scope mentions only “the liveness cache at one hour, cell granularity,” and its test may use any cached verdict (`package/children/C10.md:3,9`).

findings.title: FR-A9 acceptance bullet 2 is absent from the coverage map
findings.body: The map contains only FR-A9 bullet 1. The spec has a second acceptance bullet requiring the size slot to be recorded alongside the lane call, presentation call, and kind label, with its doctrine home in `issue-contract.md`. Although C2's body mentions this work, the acceptance-level allocation and final counts falsely report zero unallocated criteria.
findings.suggestion: Add FR-A9 bullet 2 with C2 as owner, then update C2's count from 45 to 46 and the total from 240 to 241.
